headline: 550 new dengue cases reported in 24 hours
summary: No deaths were recorded in the last 24 hours, but hospitalizations continue to rise across several divisions.
details: According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 550 new dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across Bangladesh in the last 24 hours.
The distribution of new cases includes 215 in the Dhaka division (outside city corporations), 102 in Chattogram, and 84 in Dhaka South City Corporation.
Other reported cases include 49 in Dhaka North City Corporation, 45 in Mymensingh, 38 in Khulna, 8 in Rangpur, 6 in Barishal, and 3 in Sylhet.
So far this year, a total of 31,380 people have been infected with dengue, with 61.8% being men and 38.2% being women.
Out of the total infected, 29,212 patients have recovered and been discharged from hospitals.
The total number of dengue-related deaths in the year has reached 88, according to the DGHS.

headline: 7 children die in 24 hours as measles death toll rises to 950
summary: The DGHS reports a surge in suspected cases, with over 152,000 people affected nationwide this year.
details: Seven children died with measles-like symptoms within a 24-hour window, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
This brings the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths in Bangladesh to 950 this year.
The DGHS classified the seven most recent fatalities as suspected measles deaths, raising the total suspected death toll to 851.
Laboratory-confirmed deaths remain at 99, while 73 new confirmed cases were recorded in the last 24 hours.
Nationwide, the number of suspected measles cases has reached 152,736, with 1,098 new suspected cases reported in a single day.
Since March 15, a total of 133,573 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country.
Of those hospitalized, the DGHS reports that 128,765 patients have recovered.
